title: We Are South Maui: Community Plan Advisory Committee Meeting of February 22, 2023

recap.headline: South Maui plan advisory committee adopts watershed, wetland and dune actions
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee met to keep writing actions for the Mauka to Mākaʻi Watershed Management section of the South Maui Community Plan. Four people testified, raising stormwater quality, wetlands as green infrastructure, riparian fencing, an unused Pi’ilani Village drainage basin, and the Ridge to Reef wording. Members adopted actions 4.03 through 4.11. These include a stormwater quality program, monitoring and enforcement of gulch and culvert clearing, returning diverted streams such as Kanaio Stream in Māʻalaea, a regional stormwater park, implementing the Southwest Maui Watershed Plan, and dune programs for North Kīhei and Māʻalaea. Several questions went to Planning staff without answers, including what the law requires of private owners for gulch clearing and what County land lies in the gulches mauka of the highway. Action 4.12 on near-shore water monitoring was still unfinished when the recording ran out.

parts.title: Opening, roll call and process concerns
presented: Quorum confirmed; three members absent and one excused.
Planning staff said the committee is seeking an extension. Staff blamed delays on the holidays and staffing changes in the office.
Corporation counsel could not attend because of County Council meetings.

answered.said: Staff acknowledged members' frustration with agendas and scheduling. A sidebar meeting is planned to improve communication.
The chair will ask Planning for more corporation counsel presence at meetings. The chair proposed a separate online meeting with counsel so it does not crowd the next agenda.

next.what: Separate online meeting with corporation counsel
Next meeting with two guest speakers and six actions on iwi kūpuna

parts.title: Public testimony on Mauka to Mākaʻi watershed management

raised.concern: Action items do not clearly link to and implement the plan's policies.
Policy changes from the last meeting were not posted online; the testifier asked how to get a copy.
Support for protecting riparian zones with feral ungulate fencing and plants. One speaker noted that suitable non-invasive, non-native plants should also be allowed.
Support using R1 recycled water on the landscape to reduce fire risk, recharge aquifers and feed livestock.
Action 4.11 should name the Ridge to Reef initiative 'or similar nonprofit entity' so other groups could fill the role.
Action 4.03 should call for a stormwater quality program, not just drainage. Kīhei has no MS4 permit like Kahului and Pāʻia.
The plan's definition of green infrastructure is too narrow and should include wetlands, constructed wetlands, streams and open space.
Spread stormwater across the watershed instead of channeling it into one gulch. Use the unused Pi’ilani Village drainage basin and stop filling in flood zones.
Worry about plans to intercept Waipuilani Gulch water and divert it into Kūlanihākoʻi Gulch, which is already overburdened.

answered.said: The Public Works director said at the January 25 meeting that intercepting water mauka of the highway at Waipuilani Gulch could be done fairly soon. The vice chair suggested the testifier watch that meeting.

parts.title: Committee discussion: runoff and drainage actions 4.03 to 4.05
presented: 4.03 adopted: develop a stormwater quality management program plan to protect water quality from runoff. The Kahului-Pāʻia reference was dropped because Kīhei is below the population threshold that triggers an MS4 permit.
4.04 adopted: develop monitoring programs to regularly maintain and clear sediment basins and culverts in mauka upland areas.
4.04a adopted: develop programs to monitor and enforce clearing of gulches, sediment basins and culverts, aimed at private property.
4.05 adopted: green infrastructure modifications, natural infrastructure and nature-based solutions along South Kīhei Road.

answered.said: Private landowner duties may fit better as a policy. Staff will get back on what the law requires and on what County land is in the gulches.
Private owners are legally responsible, but sediment from hundreds of acres upstream is beyond their control. Departments may need to work together.
Members discussed how plan language defines green infrastructure and added natural infrastructure and nature-based solutions to 4.05.

next.what: Planning staff to report on private property owners' legal duty to clear gulches and on County-owned land in gulches mauka of the highway

parts.title: Committee discussion: forest, streams and new watershed actions
presented: 4.06 adopted: upland forest conservation including dryland forest, plus soil protection through feral ungulate fencing and invasive species control.
New action adopted to identify, prioritize and return diverted streams such as Kanaio Stream in Māʻalaea to their natural paths.
New actions adopted: develop and implement a regional stormwater park, implement the Southwest Maui Watershed Plan, and establish a mauka-to-mākaʻi watershed advisory group.

New action adopted to establish and implement a watershed-wide water quality monitoring program. A program requiring Planning and Public Works to follow watershed plans when issuing permits was also moved.

answered.said: Added feral ungulate fencing and invasive species control to 4.06.
Staff could not say whether Public Works has a program to apply watershed plans to permits. Staff later said such a program does not really exist and the idea is reasonable.

parts.title: Committee discussion: wetland restoration and access (4.07, 4.08)
presented: 4.07 adopted: create and implement a South Maui wetland preservation and restoration program.
4.08 passed by show of hands: support, fund and expand wetland restoration projects, with low-impact managed pedestrian access where appropriate.
A member objected that dropping bike and pedestrian paths weakens beach access for local people. Another member offered to bring a separate action on reopening blocked beach access.

next.what: Planning to find where a beach-access action on reopening blocked access points belongs in the plan

parts.title: Committee discussion: dunes, dune staffing and Ridge to Reef (4.09 to 4.11)
presented: 4.09 adopted: a comprehensive dune restoration program for South Maui with a focus on North Kīhei.
4.09a adopted: develop and implement a plan and program for sand dune preservation at Haycraft Park and Māʻalaea Bay beach.
4.10 adopted: expand funding for dune management coordinator roles and for dune protection strategies. A member reported South Maui Parks plans three new dune positions.
4.11 adopted: a South Maui Ridge to Reef initiative to reduce land-based pollution harming coral reefs.

answered.said: Members discussed wording 4.11 to allow 'another entity such as a nonprofit,' noting Ridge to Reef is a coalition, not a nonprofit.

next.what: South Maui Parks hiring three dune management positions

parts.title: Near-shore water monitoring (4.12) and end of recording
presented: Members found 'care for all South Maui near-shore waters' too vague and narrowed it to monitoring.
Draft wording: support near-shore water quality monitoring under a Department of Health Quality Assurance Project Plan.
Planning staff warned of a hard stop at 9:30 p.m. because recording space was running out; the item was not finished.

next.what: Final wording for 4.12 to be provided by a committee member

open_questions.question: Are private property owners already required by law to keep gulches on their land clear, and how is that enforced?
What County-owned land or drainage infrastructure is in the gulches mauka of the highway?
Why was the Pi’ilani Village drainage basin never put into use?
Will policy changes adopted at the last meeting be posted, and how can the public get a copy?

not_on_tracker.topic: Silt-clogged gulches flooding North Kīhei condos and parks
not_on_tracker.why: Residents near Kūlanihākoʻi and Waiakoa gulches see repeated flooding when gulches on private land are not cleared.

not_on_tracker.topic: Beach access blocked by gates and private property
not_on_tracker.why: A member said local people can no longer reach the ocean for fishing, camping and diving.

not_on_tracker.topic: Sand dune loss in North Kīhei and Māʻalaea
not_on_tracker.why: Members described disappearing beaches and dunes that help protect shoreline roads and homes from storms and flooding.

not_on_tracker.topic: Diverted Kanaio Stream overwhelming drainage in Māʻalaea
not_on_tracker.why: A member said the old plantation diversion sends mud onto condos and into a fragile coastal ecosystem.

moments.quote: I wanted to share the thoughts of the spec members and request the extensions to get through the process.
moments.about: Planning staff said they were seeking schedule extensions so the advisory committee could finish its work on the South Maui Community Plan update.

moments.who: Chair of the South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee
moments.quote: A good plan is more important than a fast plan. This is something which could affect the lives of all of us and our kids and for generations to come.
moments.about: The committee chair explained why drafting the South Maui Community Plan update was taking longer than scheduled.

moments.who: A South Maui resident testifying on the plan's watershed actions
moments.quote: And I wanted to make the point that quality is a big issue in South Maui as well as the quantity.
moments.about: A resident asked that the plan's stormwater action address water quality, not just drainage, and the committee later adopted a stormwater quality management program action.

moments.who: A Kīhei advisory committee member who monitors local gulches
moments.quote: I fly the drone, take the pictures, and then I submit it to Gumi Public Works DSA, right? Request for service. Nothing happened.
moments.about: A first-hand account of unanswered complaints about silted private gulches, which shaped the plan's new action to monitor and enforce the clearing of gulches, sediment basins and culverts.
